papers.summary: Research on sycophancy asks whether large language models (LLMs) bend towards what their users want to hear. We ask the reverse question: when an LLM is confident, consistent, and wrong, do users bend towards it? In a within-subjects experiment, 32 participants learned up to five science topics by chatting with five assistants built on the same model (GPT-5-mini). Unknown to participants, each assistant's briefing had 0, 25, 50, 75, or 100% of its facts replaced by plausible falsehoods, and every assistant spoke with full confidence. A surprise quiz after each topic offered the correct fact, the planted falsehood, and two distractors, with a confidence rating for every answer. Across 104 quizzes and 1,040 answers, scores fell from 7.4 to 2.9 out of 10, and the planted option was chosen on 60% of falsified items against 11% of correctly taught ones (odds ratio 12.5). Transcript coding showed that whenever the assistant stated a falsehood, it was adopted about 65% of the time at every falsification level. Absorbed falsehoods were held with high confidence (8.4/10), the modeled confidence advantage of right over wrong answers vanished, and the discrimination of confidence for correctness fell from an AUROC of 0.70 to chance, while post-task trust ratings barely moved. Participants tended to return to the chat more when the assistant was worse, but returning went with more absorption, not less, and 30% of all turns pasted quiz questions back to the source being checked. The assistant itself was almost never sycophantic and never conceded under pushback. We introduce a baseline-corrected Human Deference Index to quantify this human-side sycophancy and argue that trustworthiness is a property of the human-AI pair, that sycophancy evaluations should measure both directions, and that learning interfaces must make reliability legible claim by claim.
papers.title_zh: 谁在对谁谄媚？自信的大语言模型、人类顺从与信任校准的崩塌
papers.abstract_zh: 关于谄媚（sycophancy）的研究追问的是：大语言模型（LLM）是否会迎合用户想听的内容。我们提出反向的问题：当一个LLM自信、前后一致且错误时，用户是否会迎合它？在一项被试内实验中，32名参与者通过与五个基于同一模型（GPT-5-mini）构建的助手聊天来学习最多五个科学主题。参与者并不知情的是，每个助手的简报中分别有0%、25%、50%、75%或100%的事实被替换为看似合理的虚假内容，并且每个助手都以完全的自信说话。每个主题之后进行一次突击测验，测验提供正确事实、植入的虚假内容以及两个干扰项，并要求对每个答案给出置信度评分。在104次测验和1,040个答案中，得分从十分制中的7.4下降到2.9，而在被伪造的题目上，植入选项被选择的概率为60%，相比之下，在正确讲授的题目上仅为11%（比值比12.5）。对话记录编码显示，每当助手陈述虚假内容时，无论处于哪一伪造水平，该内容都有约65%的概率被采纳。被吸收的虚假内容以高置信度被持有（8.4/10），正确答案相对于错误答案所模拟出的置信度优势消失了，置信度对正确性的区分能力从AUROC 0.70下降到随机水平，而任务后的信任评分几乎没有变化。当助手表现更差时，参与者倾向于更频繁地回到聊天中，但回访伴随的是更多吸收，而非更少；并且所有对话轮次中有30%将测验问题粘贴回正在被核查的来源。助手自身几乎从不谄媚，并且在受到反驳时从不让步。我们引入一个经基线校正的人类顺从指数（Human Deference Index）来量化这种人类一侧的谄媚，并主张可信性是人-AI配对的一种属性，谄媚评估应当测量两个方向，而学习界面必须逐条主张地使可靠性变得可辨识。

papers.title: Simulated Control Evals
papers.summary: Control evaluations measure whether safeguards can prevent an AI model from causing undesired outcomes even when it is intentionally trying to do so. These evaluations typically use purpose-built control settings and extrapolate their results to a model's deployment. However, the effectiveness of safeguards in deployment can depend on features of environments and tasks that control settings do not represent. To broaden where control evaluations can be run, we introduce simulated control evaluations (SCEs), which use a language model to simulate tool responses in place of an environment. We evaluate SCEs on LinuxArena, where execution provides ground-truth outcomes. We compare SCE prediction errors with those from a separate control setting, BashArena, and with variation in control metrics within LinuxArena. For independently sampled evaluation and deployment task sets, SCEs predict safety with a root mean squared error of 3.6 percentage points across five monitors at a 5% audit budget, compared with 10.1 for BashArena. SCEs closely reproduce distributions of attack strategies, attacker reasoning, and monitor reasoning, with over tenfold lower KL divergence from execution than BashArena. SCEs explain 78-85% of the between-environment variance in attack success, monitor scores, and safety. This accuracy is sample efficient: SCEs predict safety with less error than BashArena using fewer than 5% as many task-pair draws as the deployment task set. Strategies discovered through simulation also improve monitor performance on held-out LinuxArena attacks, outperforming BashArena and approximately matching improvement from executed strategies. These results suggest that deployment-specific SCEs can be more predictive than control evaluations executed in separate control settings.

papers.title: EpiSEM-Bench: Evaluating Safety and Evidence Recovery in LLM Agents under Missing Evidence
papers.summary: Tool-using language model agents rely on environmental facts to decide whether an action is permitted. When a tool response omits a safety-relevant fact, an agent may carry out a prohibited action even though the user request is benign and every returned statement is true. We introduce \bench{}, an executable benchmark for evaluating unsafe execution, safety boundaries, and evidence recovery in LLM agents under missing evidence. It contains 300 matched unsafe/safe task pairs across six domains. By systematically suppressing critical facts, the benchmark measures unsafe execution under critical evidence omission and determines the minimum observed failure cardinality, including failures with full evidence and cases with no observed failure after exhaustive testing. An independent audit tool tests whether agents seek missing facts and then withhold prohibited actions while completing permissible tasks. The benchmark reveals substantial variation across the ten models in omission robustness, evidence acquisition, and appropriate action. Resistance to missing evidence does not necessarily translate into useful recovery. Recovery access reduces unsafe execution for all ten models, but agents differ in whether they actively obtain the missing facts and use them to act appropriately in both worlds.

papers.title: Direct Pass@$k$ Optimization for Thought Pruning: Balancing Quality and Diversity in Test-Time Reasoning
papers.summary: Test-time scaling has emerged as a key inference strategy for reasoning models, where a model generates a large number of candidate solutions in the hope of finding at least one correct solution. Running all candidate solutions to completion can be computationally demanding, so recent work prunes the candidate pool after generating only a short prefix, committing further computation only to the surviving candidates. Existing pruning strategies divide broadly into two categories: Quality-based methods assign a score to each partial solution and discard those predicted to ultimately lead to an incorrect final solution, while diversity-based methods select partial solutions that follow different reasoning trajectories and are therefore likely to cover different final solutions. The tension between these two objectives is an instance of exploration versus exploitation, yet little to no prior work on pruning exposes this trade-off directly, let alone optimizes it. In this paper, we introduce a pruning procedure that addresses this trade-off directly by optimizing pass@$k$ over the selected solution pool. In particular, it chooses the pool to maximize the probability that at least one of its partial solutions, when continued to completion, yields a correct answer. Because this objective simultaneously rewards high-quality partial solutions and penalizes redundancy among them, quality and diversity are naturally balanced by the criterion itself rather than through separate ad-hoc design choices. On eight open-weight reasoning models, our method outperforms existing quality-based and diversity-based pruning strategies. The gains are particularly pronounced when the pruning procedure keeps a moderate number of partial solutions for continued generation, highlighting the value of directly balancing quality and diversity during pruning.

papers.title: Verified DRAM Address Mapping Reverse Engineering with Threshold Sweep
papers.summary: We propose an end-to-end software pipeline for solving and validating DRAM address mapping functions on embedded LPDDR5 systems, and we instantiate it on embedded platforms. Starting from a large latency dataset of address pairs, the pipeline first builds a latency histogram and then performs a threshold sweep to obtain candidate same-bank address pairs. For each threshold, we apply a Knock-Knock-style linear-constraint solver to recover candidate bank masks. Final bank masks are calculated using GF(2) reduced row echelon form (RREF). To verify correctness, we implement two verification stages, group verification and single function verification, inspired by prior work. Group verification checks whether bank partitions induced by the recovered masks agree with observed timing behavior. Single function verification removes one addressing function at a time and measures the resulting change in verification pass rate. Unlike approaches that return only a single inferred mapping, our workflow systematically records, for each candidate threshold, the solved bank masks and validation metrics. This pipeline supports more robust selection of bank masks on ARM-based embedded devices and provides an efficient method for reverse engineering DRAM address mapping functions and subsequent Rowhammer analysis.

papers.title: Proba: A High-Performance, Low-Traffic Probabilistic Spatial Memory Streaming Prefetcher
papers.summary: Spatial Memory Streaming (SMS) prefetchers exploit recurring spatial access patterns across memory regions to predict future accesses. Despite their effectiveness, existing SMS-based designs suffer from coarse control over aggressiveness and limited adaptability to dynamic program behavior and historical patterns. In this work, we present Proba, a feedback-directed SMS-based prefetcher that integrates probabilistic pattern updates, marginal accuracy decision-making, and pattern accumulation over several trigger features to achieve fine-grained accuracy-coverage trade-offs. When accuracy deteriorates, Proba moderates its aggressiveness to prioritize accurate prefetches; conversely, when accuracy rises, it expands its coverage. Proba achieves higher speedups than any other SMS-based prefetcher while being vastly more efficient in DRAM traffic. This culminates in a large performance gap between Proba and other techniques in multicore and DRAM-constrained scenarios without harming single-threaded throughput.

papers.title: FIGFLEX: A Mixed-Precision FP-INT GEMM Accelerator Co-Designed with Low-Bit LLM Quantization
papers.summary: Weight-only quantization keeps LLM activations in floating point and stores weights as low-bit integers, turning the dominant workload into floating-point-integer (FP-INT) general matrix multiplication. Recent quantizers reach a 2-3-bit average with mixed precision, but hardware has not kept pace: GPUs dequantize weights to FP16 before the tensor-core multiply-accumulate, and bit-parallel FP-INT accelerators run at a single weight precision, so fewer bits save memory but not computation. In this paper, we present FIGFLEX, an algorithm-hardware co-designed mixed-precision accelerator whose bit-parallel datapath scales throughput as precision falls. FIGFLEX contributes (1) a shift-add, radix-4 reformulation of FP-INT multiplication that fuses the multiply-accumulate into a unified, precision-flexible partial-product reduction and roughly halves the partial products, together with a novel INT3 optimization that reclaims the idle datapath radix-4 leaves at that precision; and (2) a mixed-precision quantizer that assigns each channel group its bit-width according to the error GPTQ cannot compensate, with a per-input-channel column scaling whose power-of-two normalization keeps the scaled activations out of the FP16 subnormal range, so that the quantized model maps directly onto FIGFLEX's datapath with the same accuracy as on a GPU. On LLaMA-2-7B, FIGFLEX attains 5.85 and 8.77 WikiText-2 perplexity at 3- and 2-bit average precision, lower than GPTQ, AWQ, SliM-LLM, AMQ, and QuIP# (without fine-tuning), while delivering 1.56x and 1.42x higher whole-chip throughput per area on the linear GEMMs of a 3-bit mixed-precision model than AxCore and FIGLUT, respectively.

papers.title: HDLouvain: High-Throughput Incremental Clustering for Hyperdimensional Data
papers.summary: Modern shotgun proteomics generates tens of thousands of tandem mass spectra per hour, producing hundreds of gigabytes of data that strain conventional clustering pipelines. DBSCAN and hierarchical agglomerative clustering (HAC) offer flexible similarity search, but DBSCAN is unstable across varying data densities, HAC costs $O(n^2)$, and both yield poor cluster quality. Graph-based methods such as Louvain produce high-quality clusters but scale poorly on streaming data. We observe that Louvain's poor scalability can be resolved without sacrificing its quality, and present HDLouvain, which combines Louvain community detection with the bit-parallel similarity computation of hyperdimensional computing (HDC). HDLouvain partitions a bootstrap fraction of the stream into precursor-mass buckets, applies Louvain to each bucket's kNN similarity graph, and condenses each community into a single binary hypervector by bitwise-majority bundling rather than iterative centroid recomputation. New spectra are assigned by a GPU-accelerated Hamming distance lookup against representatives in their mass bucket, or seed a new cluster when no match meets a similarity threshold $τ$, so the partition grows incrementally without full re-clustering. On five PRIDE datasets (0.99M to 21.13M spectra), sweeping the bootstrap fraction $α$ from 0.2 to 0.9 exposes an explicit, monotonic throughput-fidelity trade-off. On PXD003258, speedup ranges from 4.5x at $α=0.3$ to 1.65x at $α=0.7$. Modularity rises from 0.75-0.76 at $α=0.2$ to 0.95-0.97 at $α=0.9$, never more than 8% below full static recomputation. The Louvain stage achieves 0.86-0.93 normalized mutual information (NMI) on LFR benchmark networks with 30k to 2M nodes, whereas DBSCAN and HAC degrade to 0.57.

papers.title: SnakeCharmer: Orchestrating Utility, Timeliness, and Placement in GPU Prefetching
papers.summary: GPUs rely on massive thread-level parallelism to tolerate long memory latency, yet they still suffer severe stalls when many warps simultaneously wait for data from the memory system. Address-prediction-based GPU prefetchers can mitigate such stalls, but accurate prediction alone does not guarantee performance improvement: a predicted prefetch becomes beneficial only if it is worth issuing, arrives at the right time, and is retained without harmful interference. Because these requirements interact, optimizing any single dimension in isolation can simply move the bottleneck to another. We capture these requirements with a predicted-prefetch-to-realized-benefit perspective and propose SnakeCharmer, a unified backend prefetch-control framework for address-prediction-based GPU prefetchers. SnakeCharmer separates address prediction from prefetch realization: the frontend predictor generates prefetch candidates, while the backend control path jointly controls utility, timeliness, and placement by determining whether each candidate should be issued, when it should be issued, and where the returned data should be retained. SnakeCharmer realizes this control path with zero-value-aware filtering for utility, hierarchical feedback-driven distance tuning for timeliness, and a register-assisted prefetch buffer for placement. We design and implement SnakeCharmer primarily on top of Snake, and adapt the same backend-control principles to APOGEE to demonstrate that SnakeCharmer's benefits are not limited to a single frontend predictor. On an A100 GPU model, SnakeCharmer improves performance/energy efficiency by 12.8%/20.8% over Snake and by 1.7%/3.2% over APOGEE, with modest hardware overhead.

papers.title: Ray-by-Ray: Fine-Grained Resource Management for GPU Ray Tracing Units
papers.summary: Ray tracing (RT) generates photorealistic images by simulating the physical behavior of light as it interacts with surfaces in a virtual scene. In film production and high-end rendering pipelines, this technique computes global illumination, reflections, refractions, and soft shadows by tracing millions of light rays per frame and accurately modeling their bounces and attenuation. Contemporary GPUs incorporate specialized ray tracing hardware to accelerate key operations in the traversal pipeline. By accelerating these stages in hardware, the unit enables real-time ray tracing for complex scenes that previously required offline computation. However, ray tracing introduces substantial control and data divergence. Each ray may traverse a different set of nodes in the acceleration structure, encounter distinct materials, or terminate at varying depths. This irregularity reduces thread coherence and exposes a fundamental disparity between the GPU SIMT and per-thread execution model of dedicated RT units, where each ray progresses independently. In this work, we seek to validate assumptions made in open-source infrastructure and identify potential inefficiencies in resource management within the ray tracing pipeline. To address inefficiency caused by mismatches between SIMT and RT granularities, we propose Ray-by-Ray, which decomposes on-chip buffers into the granularity of individual rays and introduces lightweight management structures that enable more warps to run in parallel without increasing buffer capacity. This approach improves ray tracing unit utilization and increases memory-level parallelism. Experimental results show that Ray-by-Ray achieves an average performance improvement of 1.91x over the baseline, with an area overhead of 0.19\%.

papers.title: Hyperreduction accelerates finite element model updating for the discovery of neural materials
papers.summary: Finite element model updating is among the most general approaches to discover constitutive models from structural experiments: since the displacement field is computed rather than measured, it accommodates arbitrary geometries, boundary conditions, and sparse or noisy data. However, every loss evaluation requires a nonlinear finite element solve per load step, and training neural materials requires many such evaluations. Intrusive model order reduction lowers this cost while retaining boundary conditions and variational structure. How can a reduced model remain accurate while the network weights change at every training step? We combine proper orthogonal decomposition and energy-conserving sampling and weighting with adjoint sensitivities of the reduced model, and adapt both the trial space and the sampled elements along the optimization path. The constitutive law is a polyconvex neural network: a logarithmic normalization term, together with a zero-anchored input convex architecture and a growth term, renders the energy polyconvex, coercive, and non-negative by construction, independent of the trained weights. We demonstrate the approach on two experimental datasets and one synthetic three-dimensional example. For a two-phase specimen, training time decreases from nine hours to 41 minutes compared with a full-order identification, without loss of accuracy. In the three-dimensional example, six modes replace 48 672 degrees of freedom, 116 of 15 625 elements suffice to evaluate the internal forces, and training takes 13 minutes. In all cases, the identified material reproduces the measured reaction force and predicts the displacement field from the force alone. Hyperreduction makes the discovery of neural materials from structural data affordable while retaining the advantages of finite element model updating.

papers.title: Structure-preserving reduced-order models of thin panels in supersonic and hypersonic flow
papers.summary: We build structure-preserving reduced-order models for both challenge problems of the AePW-4 High-Speed Working Group. They are a clamped thin panel at Mach 1.92 (RC-19) and a cantilever plate at Mach 5.85 (HyMAX). The published data for each case hold no time-resolved response and no repeated runs. The physics must therefore be carried by the form of the model. One construction gives two models per problem. A Ritz-Galerkin reference model describes the plate. A learned model keeps the reference model's exact potential, fits the remaining generalized forces, and trains only a dissipation that cannot add energy. Its energy balance holds for any weights by construction. On the trained model the worst relative residual is 2.2e-15. On RC-19, shock relations predict a pressure ratio of 1.521 across the panel. Pressure-sensitive paint measured the same value. Thirty runs of the learned model place the mean dominant frequency within 1.0% of the measured 236 Hz. At one periodic and one chaotic condition, the learned model reproduces the response regime of a published reduced-order model in all sixteen runs. It does so without that model's 113 Hz spectral peak, which the measurements do not show. Measured displacements can also correct the chaotic response through one more force that respects the energy balance. We tested this on synthetic data at the experiment's 5 kHz sampling rate. The state error is 1.25% of the panel thickness without noise and 3.5% with 10 micrometers of noise. On HyMAX the learned model follows the reference model's trailing-edge displacement for 65 ms with a relative error of 3.7%. These results show that a model whose structure carries the physics can match measured flutter behavior when the available data cannot train it.

papers.title: Measuring Research Progress and Linguistic Inclusion in Low-Resource Languages
papers.summary: Large Language Models (LLMs) have accelerated research on low-resource and multilingual NLP, but their effectiveness in creating an equitable landscape remains unmapped. We analyze 1,158 peer-reviewed open-access papers published between 2020 and 2025, examining research attention to low-resource languages (LRLs) and representation across language and speaker populations. To assess linguistic inclusion beyond publication counts, we introduce the Linguistic Inclusion Framework (LIF), a multidimensional framework that measures linguistic inclusion in four dimensions: research growth, representation expansion, representation continuity, and distributional equity. While annual publications grew from 52 to 415, a 5.4X increase in their ACL Anthology publication share, this growth largely concentrated on represented languages rather than expanding coverage of underrepresented languages. Further analysis shows that languages spoken in Asia account for 64.1% of speakers across LRLs we analyze but receive only 46.7% of the language representation share (0.7X their proportional share), while European languages receive 5.3X their proportional share. At the country level, linguistically diverse regions such as sub-Saharan Africa and Southeast Asia show the lowest language coverage ratios. Applying the framework at the continental level, we find that no region scores well on all four dimensions, showing that research growth alone is not a reliable metric of progress toward equitable and inclusive language technology\footnote{We will release all collected and annotated data for research purposes}.
papers.title_zh: 衡量低资源语言中的研究进展与语言包容性
papers.abstract_zh: 大语言模型（LLMs）加速了低资源与多语言自然语言处理（NLP）的研究，但其在构建公平格局方面的有效性仍未被描绘。我们分析了2020年至2025年间发表的1,158篇经同行评审的开放获取论文，考察了对低资源语言（LRLs）的研究关注度以及在语言和说话人群体上的代表性。为了在论文数量之外评估语言包容性，我们提出了语言包容性框架（LIF），这是一个多维框架，从四个维度衡量语言包容性：研究增长、代表性扩展、代表性连续性和分布公平性。尽管年度发表量从52篇增长到415篇，其在ACL Anthology发表份额中实现了5.4倍的增长，但这种增长主要集中在已被代表的语言上，而非扩展对代表性不足语言的覆盖。进一步分析显示，在我们分析的低资源语言中，亚洲使用的语言占说话人总数的64.1%，却仅获得46.7%的语言代表性份额（为其按比例应得份额的0.7倍），而欧洲语言获得的份额是其按比例应得份额的5.3倍。在国家层面，撒哈拉以南非洲和东南亚等语言多样性丰富的地区表现出最低的语言覆盖率。将该框架应用于洲际层面，我们发现没有任何地区在全部四个维度上表现良好，这表明仅凭研究增长并不是衡量朝着公平且包容的语言技术取得进展的可靠指标\footnote{我们将发布所有收集和标注的数据以供研究使用}。

papers.title: AQL-Lite: Enabling Efficient Knowledge Acquisition for Arabic LLMs via Data-Centric Continual Pretraining
papers.summary: Training Arabic large language models faces challenges from noisy web data, dialectal variation, and the high cost of continual pretraining (CPT). We introduce AQL-Lite (AQL: Arabic Quality Language), a time- and resource-efficient framework for adapting a multilingual LLM to Modern Standard Arabic (MSA). AQL-Lite couples a quality-first curation pipeline (structural cleaning, heuristic and model-based filtering, MSA selection, and deduplication) with a partial-parameter CPT recipe that trains RS-LoRA adapters across the network together with the last eight transformer blocks and the embedding matrix, under layer-wise learning rates. At a matched 1B-token budget, CPT on AQL-curated data raises a four-benchmark Arabic mean by 3.51 points over CPT on raw web text, which yields no gain over the base model. In a controlled 5B-token comparison, AQL-Lite recovers 94% of the gain of full-parameter CPT (mean 73.19 vs. 73.58) in 52% of the wall-clock time and outperforms adapter-only baselines on every benchmark, and a component ablation shows that adapters, unfrozen blocks, and embedding training each contribute. Scaled to 40B MSA tokens and instruction-tuned on one million examples, the resulting 12B model scores 75.3 on the seven-benchmark Open Arabic LLM Leaderboard v2 (OALL v2) suite. These results suggest that partial-parameter CPT on a carefully curated corpus is a practical route to efficient MSA adaptation.
papers.title_zh: AQL-Lite：通过以数据为中心的持续预训练为阿拉伯语 LLM 实现高效知识获取
papers.abstract_zh: 训练阿拉伯语大语言模型面临来自噪声网页数据、方言差异以及持续预训练（CPT）高成本的挑战。我们提出 AQL-Lite（AQL：Arabic Quality Language），这是一个在时间和资源上高效的框架，用于将多语言 LLM 适配到现代标准阿拉伯语（MSA）。AQL-Lite 将质量优先的数据整理流水线（结构化清洗、启发式和基于模型的过滤、MSA 选择以及去重）与部分参数 CPT 方案相结合，该方案在网络中训练 RS-LoRA 适配器，同时训练最后八个 transformer 块和嵌入矩阵，并采用逐层学习率。在匹配的 10 亿 token 预算下，与在原始网页文本上进行 CPT 相比，在 AQL 整理的数据上进行 CPT 将四个基准的阿拉伯语平均值提高了 3.51 分，而在原始网页文本上进行 CPT 相对于基础模型没有带来任何增益。在一项受控的 50 亿 token 比较中，AQL-Lite 在 52% 的挂钟时间内恢复了全参数 CPT 增益的 94%（均值 73.19 对 73.58），并且在每个基准上都优于仅使用适配器的基线；组件消融表明，适配器、未冻结块和嵌入训练各自都有贡献。扩展到 400 亿 MSA token 并在 100 万个示例上进行指令微调后，所得的 12B 模型在包含七个基准的 Open Arabic LLM Leaderboard v2（OALL v2）套件上得分为 75.3。这些结果表明，在精心整理的语料上进行部分参数 CPT 是实现高效 MSA 适配的一条切实可行的路径。

papers.title: Consistency Is Not Validity: Self-Rewarded Moral Argumentation Makes Language Models Decisive but Pliable
papers.summary: LLMs are increasingly consulted for moral judgment. We aim to improve performance on such tasks by rewarding good arguments, on the premise that arguing well increases the likelihood of judging well. We train a reinforcement learning policy initialized from a state-of-the-art language model in a self-judged tournament with masked thinking: the generated arguments are judged pairwise on argument quality by the policy itself. As an empirical basis, we extract authentic dilemmas from classic novels, using a logic solver to verify that each constitutes a conflict. We show that our judge rates argument quality like human annotators, and the policy then adopts the language register that it rewards. Testing on the external benchmarks MoralChoice, ELEPHANT, and MORABLES, we find that the policy becomes more decisive and invariant to the order in which options are presented, but sycophancy and reframing remain a challenge to validity. Two ablation studies with synthetic dilemmas and unmasked thinking match the reordering gains, but show a weaker register shift and higher sycophancy. We conclude that consistency is not validity: consistency under reordering can be optimized without improving the moral judgment it is meant to signal.

papers.title: CiteAnchor: Source-Aware Grounding for Hallucinated Citation Detection and Resolution
papers.summary: Hallucinated citations make it harder to trace sources and verify the evidence behind scientific claims. Detecting them is difficult because bibliographic records can be incomplete or differ across source types and publication versions. A plausible match alone neither validates the citation nor establishes its underlying source. We introduce CiteResolve, a benchmark of 423 real-world hallucinated citations annotated for source recoverability. We further propose CiteAnchor, a source-aware grounding framework that adapts retrieval and field-level verification to each source type and separately determines citation validity and whether a unique source can be recovered. On an existing detection benchmark, CiteAnchor achieves 0.841 F1 with GPT-5.6 Luna and 0.784 with an open-weight backbone, outperforming the baseline with the same backbones by 7.9 and 36.8 points. On CiteResolve, it achieves 74.7% and 70.7% end-to-end task success, outperforming the corresponding web search baselines by 16.3 and 65.3 percentage points. Our code and data are available at https://github.com/oldwizard7/CiteANCHOR_code.

papers.title: Climbing the Ladder: Automating Data Pipelines and Reproducing Baselines in Low-Resource Settings
papers.summary: The massively multilingual translation systems that now include Sicilian learned it from noisy, non-standardised web text. To obtain better translation quality, we redevelop the small neural machine translation (NMT) system that Wdowiak customized for Sicilian. We rebuild on maintained software the extraction of the parallel text from the PDFs of the bilingual journal Arba Sicula, whose sentences are aligned by a language-agnostic sentence encoder with thresholds tuned against an existing hand alignment and then filtered for the typical errors of automatic alignment. Furthermore, the tokenization and the desinence-biased subword segmentation of the original system are ported to a Perl-free implementation, and all the results are measured on a frozen test set drawn from the journal. We compare small Transformers trained from scratch with the pretrained NLLB model adapted by low-rank fine-tuning, in both directions and with Italian as a closely related bridge language, and we adapt to the pretrained model the reverse-training recipe of the original system, i.e., a stage on forward-scored back-translations of the web Sicilian followed by a stage on the curated literary text. The pretrained model is by far the better of the two, and the staged training improves the translation into Sicilian more than the translation from it. On the test set of the original system, and in the tokenized space in which it was scored, the staged model with a larger adapter and more back-translations is above the reverse-training recipe in the directions that involve English and below it between Sicilian and Italian. Yet, a multilingual adapter degrades the directions on which it was not trained, which limits its use as a general multilingual model.

papers.title: MemPlan: Memory-Conditioned PDDL Planning for Partially Observable Text Environments
papers.summary: LLM agents are flexible in language interaction, but using them as long-horizon planners is costly and prone to hallucinated or invalid actions. This paper targets a different role for LLMs: constrained bridges between language and symbolic planning. We propose MemPlan, a memory-conditioned PDDL planning framework for partially observable interactive text environments. MemPlan keeps the PDDL domain fixed and reconstructs the PDDL problem at each step from parsed observations, candidate hypotheses, and interaction memory. Positive graph memory assigns relevance-based action costs to candidate hypotheses for missing objects, locations, or conditions, guiding the planner toward more plausible checks. Negative memory records execution-refuted assumptions and compiles them into exclusion constraints, preventing repeated attempts at candidates already contradicted by feedback. A unified schema-conditioned language--symbol interface, trained offline with supervised fine-tuning, connects text environments to the planning loop through observation-to-fact parsing and symbolic-action-to-command grounding. Experiments on TextWorld, ALFWorld, and Robotouille show that MemPlan improves task completion and step efficiency over language-only and PDDL-aware baselines, while substantially reducing online token cost compared with LLM-planning baselines such as ReAct. The same fine-tuned interface is also reused across TextWorld task types without task-specific fine-tuning. Our code and data are available at: https://github.com/tewiSong/MemPlan.

papers.title: SIM-UT: A User Simulation based Evaluation Framework for Medical Triage Chatbots
papers.summary: LLM-based chat agents are increasingly used for complex, multi-turn, multilingual medical triage in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs), yet evaluation methods focus on single-turn, English-only benchmarks that primarily test the chatbots' knowledge. In practice, users are often confused, overwhelmed, or emotionally vulnerable, giving unclear, misspelled single-word answers or long messages in regional dialects, and the context of a conversation can shift rapidly. We propose SIM-UT (Simulation of User Behaviour for Triage), a multi-turn, simulation-based evaluation method that identifies ecologically valid, contextually relevant failure modes of LLM-based triage chat agents. Using SIM-UT, we evaluated three real-world WhatsApp-based health chatbots: a respiratory screening programme in India, a hearing health support programme in South Africa, and a diabetes and lifestyle coaching agent in Kenya. We compared a medically fine-tuned open model (MedGemma) against general-purpose frontier models (ChatGPT and Claude) across 5,000+ multilingual simulated conversation turns grounded in the personas, constraints, and communication patterns of the real user populations, over 2-4 iterative rounds. A key failure mode emerged in both model families: de-escalation risk. The agents initially identified medical emergencies correctly, but when the user minimised the symptoms without introducing new clinical information, they de-escalated, exhibiting clinically dangerous sycophancy, for example agreeing that vaginal bleeding in pregnancy was "not a problem" or that decreased fetal movements at 32 weeks "can be normal". We recommend user simulation-based behavioural evaluation, grounded in real user context and covering adversarial and edge cases, as standard practice for triage chatbots in production, so that safeguards can be added before deployment or in subsequent iterations.

papers.title: Self-Assessment Reinforcement Learning for Search-State Awareness in Retrieval-Augmented Large Language Models
papers.summary: Recent advances in search agents have enabled large language models to tackle complex tasks by retrieving and synthesizing external information. However, existing search agents often lack search-state awareness, i.e., the ability to recognize what information has been obtained and what remains missing, leading to hallucinated reasoning and prematurely terminated search. To address this limitation, we propose Self-Assessment Reinforcement Learning (SARL), a reinforcement learning framework in which models learn to recognize their own search state during training and improve their search behavior accordingly, without requiring additional assessment at test time. SARL achieves this through a dual reward design that captures the corrective effect of each assessment while penalizing excessive reliance on it, jointly encouraging effective and efficient search trajectories. Under this setup, SARL achieves a 24.3% relative improvement over the strongest baseline, with average gains of 35.9% on multi-hop reasoning and 27.9% on deep research benchmarks against the strongest per-benchmark baselines. SARL further surpasses methods built on auxiliary supervision or multi-agent coordination, despite operating as a standalone RL framework with no inference-time scaffolding. Beyond final performance, SARL maintains training stability under extended search horizons, a regime where existing methods consistently degrade, enabling sustained gains as task complexity grows.
papers.title_zh: 面向检索增强大型语言模型搜索状态感知的自我评估强化学习
papers.abstract_zh: 近年来搜索智能体的进展使大型语言模型能够通过检索和综合外部信息来处理复杂任务。然而，现有搜索智能体往往缺乏搜索状态感知，即识别已获得哪些信息以及仍缺失哪些信息的能力，从而导致幻觉性推理和过早终止搜索。为解决这一局限，我们提出自我评估强化学习（SARL），一种强化学习框架，其中模型在训练期间学习识别自身的搜索状态并据此改进其搜索行为，而无需在测试时进行额外评估。SARL通过双奖励设计实现这一点，该设计捕捉每次评估的纠正效果，同时惩罚对其的过度依赖，共同鼓励有效且高效的搜索轨迹。在此设置下，SARL相对于最强基线实现了24.3%的相对提升，相对于最强的各基准基线，在多跳推理上平均提升35.9%，在深度研究基准上平均提升27.9%。SARL进一步超越了基于辅助监督或多智能体协调的方法，尽管它作为一个独立的强化学习框架运行，且没有推理时脚手架。除了最终性能之外，SARL在扩展的搜索视界下保持训练稳定性，而现有方法在这一情形下持续退化，从而随着任务复杂度增长实现持续增益。

papers.title: Rethinking the Evaluation of LLM Fact-Checkers
papers.summary: Large language models (LLMs) are widely used to answer factual questions, but their answers can contain errors and must be fact-checked claim by claim. Yet the resulting score depends on three design decisions: which questions the claims answer, under what conditions each claim is judged, and which sources count as evidence. No existing benchmark specifies all three. We introduce JSFactCheckBench, a Japanese benchmark that specifies all three, with 1,913 claims from LLM answers to questions about misleading information that circulated on Japanese social media, each annotated for factuality at a reference time and for importance to the question, using evidence from preselected Web sources. Across six LLMs, all verify claims directly answering the question less accurately than supplementary claims, a gap that aggregate scores obscure. Scores also drop when models must locate the relevant content in longer or multiple sources and, for all four open models, when the surrounding question and response are added. These weaknesses are visible only because the benchmark records the conditions behind each label. A benchmark that leaves them implicit cannot reveal them.
papers.title_zh: 重新思考 LLM 事实核查器的评估
papers.abstract_zh: 大型语言模型（LLM）被广泛用于回答事实性问题，但其答案可能包含错误，必须逐条主张进行事实核查。然而，由此得到的分数取决于三个设计决策：这些主张回答的是哪些问题、每条主张在何种条件下被判定，以及哪些来源可计为证据。现有基准均未同时明确这三点。我们提出 JSFactCheckBench，这是一个同时明确上述三点的日语基准，包含 1,913 条主张，这些主张来自 LLM 对有关在日本社交媒体上传播的误导性信息的问题的回答；每条主张均使用来自预先选定的网络来源的证据，标注其在参考时间点的事实性及其对问题的重要性。在六个 LLM 上，所有模型对直接回答该问题的主张的验证准确率都低于对补充性主张的验证准确率，而聚合分数掩盖了这一差距。当模型必须在更长或多个来源中定位相关内容时，分数也会下降；而对于所有四个开放模型，当加入周围的问题和回答时，分数同样会下降。这些弱点之所以可见，仅仅是因为该基准记录了每个标签背后的条件。而将这些条件隐而不显的基准则无法揭示它们。

papers.title: Behind Aggregate Scores: What Systematically Varying Arena-Hard's LLM Judge Reveals
papers.summary: LLM judges are used to determine which of two answers is better. Trusting these verdicts requires knowing how repeatable they are and how much they depend on the judge's instructions. We show that similar aggregate scores can conceal substantial changes in individual verdicts, both when the same setup is repeated and when the instructions change. Using 500 Arena-Hard v2.0 prompts with two models' answers held fixed, we run GPT-4.1 as the judge under all eight combinations of criteria, output format and task framing, and repeat every setup unchanged at temperature zero on a pinned model version. Rerunning the default setup moves the aggregate score by about one point but changes the win/tie/loss outcome on 21.2% of prompts. Instruction changes introduce further sensitivity: in one setup, which asks for the verdict without reasoning and also drops several other instructions, outcomes change on 28.2 percentage points more prompts than the two setups' unchanged reruns do on average, and the aggregate score falls by 4.09 points. In another, where the criteria prioritise accuracy, outcomes change on 6.7 percentage points more prompts by the same comparison, while the aggregate score barely moves. A stable aggregate score therefore does not establish that individual verdicts are repeatable. This distinction matters when those verdicts are used as preference labels or to assess individual responses. Evaluations that rely on individual verdicts should repeat each setup they use and report both aggregate scores and prompt-level agreement.

papers.title: Protegrity-PII Technical Report
papers.summary: We present Protegrity-PII, a new PII decision model for structured and unstructured text. Protegrity-PII achieves a typed recall of 0.915 with a precision of 0.907 on a new benchmark we propose, PII-SCOPE. Our model processes text in 0.49 seconds per million characters at \$0.0005 per million characters on a single RTX 6000 using batched inference. Due in part to the expansive nature of the entity type taxonomy used in training, Protegrity-PII achieves superior out-of-distribution generalization when benchmarked against a selection of state of the art models and datasets.

papers.title: IFC-MCQ: Automatically Generating Multiple-Choice Benchmarks for Evaluating LLM Agents on IFC Data Retrieval
papers.summary: Industry Foundation Classes (IFC), the standard for building information exchange in architecture, engineering, and construction (AEC), is increasingly queried through large language models (LLMs) using natural language. Evaluating these systems at scale is difficult because free-text answers require costly human or LLM-based review. We propose IFC-MCQ, a method that automatically generates multiple-choice benchmarks from IFC files for exact option-set grading. The taxonomy covers 15 categories and 36 subtypes across four groups, with answer keys derived from the file and distractors constructed from file-derived values or predefined rules. We applied IFC-MCQ to IFC models of varying sizes and modelling characteristics to assess generation coverage and evaluated two agentic configurations on selected models using tool- and code-based retrieval. The evaluation exposed category-specific failure modes and showed that performance can vary with the source IFC model and retrieval interface. IFC-MCQ enables scalable benchmarking of LLM-based IFC retrieval in AEC workflows.
papers.title_zh: IFC-MCQ：自动生成用于评估 LLM 智能体在 IFC 数据检索任务上的多项选择基准
papers.abstract_zh: 工业基础类（IFC）是建筑、工程与施工（AEC）领域建筑信息交换的标准，目前正越来越多地通过大语言模型（LLM）以自然语言进行查询。大规模评估这些系统十分困难，因为自由文本答案需要昂贵的人工评审或基于 LLM 的评审。我们提出 IFC-MCQ，一种从 IFC 文件自动生成多项选择基准、以实现精确选项集评分的方法。该分类体系涵盖四个组别下的 15 个类别和 36 个子类型，答案键由文件导出，干扰项则基于文件导出的值或预定义规则构建。我们将 IFC-MCQ 应用于具有不同规模和建模特征的 IFC 模型，以评估生成覆盖率，并在选定的模型上使用基于工具和基于代码的检索方式评估了两种智能体配置。评估揭示了特定类别的失败模式，并表明性能会随源 IFC 模型和检索接口的不同而变化。IFC-MCQ 支持在 AEC 工作流中对基于 LLM 的 IFC 检索进行可扩展的基准测试。

papers.title: What the Specification Did Not Say: Specification-Oracle Gaps in Test-Graded Coding-Agent Benchmarks
papers.summary: Coding-agent benchmarks often describe a task in natural language but grade it with tests taken from the upstream project. Passing those tests can require information the description never states: a constant's name, a module path, an exact message. We call this a specification-oracle gap: where it exists, a benchmark also measures whether an agent reproduces upstream implementation details. We formalise the gap, including the inconsistencies that chains of dependent tasks add, and build a static audit for five languages that classifies every name-, path- and literal-level dependency of every scored test (held-out precision 89.2%, recall 92.9%). On SWE-Milestone (98 graded milestones, 35 published runs), 25 milestones contain a test that depends on an unstated, non-inferable name or path. Build units with such a dependency fail in 80.6% of runs, against 48.4% for comparable units without one, and withholding a single hidden name from the reference stops its unit's tests from compiling in 126 of 128 cases. The leaderboard's ranking is robust to removing the affected tests, but they shift scores within repositories and favour agents that reproduce upstream names. Across four further benchmarks, prevalence appears to follow construction: a third or more of the tasks are affected where specifications are release notes or LLM summaries, almost none where tasks are screened or written for their tests; how much a gap costs depends on how the harness grades. We release the audit, corrected filter lists and specification addenda.

papers.title: Compiling Autoregressive LLM Control into Policy-Exact Parallel Inference for Hierarchical RAG
papers.summary: Large language models increasingly act as controllers in structured decision pipelines, yet their decisions are still executed by autoregressive text decoding. Hierarchical RAG is one such setting: at each frontier of a document tree, an LLM commits to $b$ of $k$ sections under an input-dependent action grammar, executed as either failure-prone free-form JSON or reliable but strictly serial grammar-constrained generation. We show that this serialization is unnecessary for bounded-horizon control: the reachable future forms a shallow action-prefix tree, which we compile --- one root prefill plus one tree-causal probe evaluate every prefix-conditioned action distribution with serial decoding's tokens, positions, and causal ancestry. A prefix-state lemma makes compiled control policy-exact in exact arithmetic: the same policy with a two-forward critical path and zero output tokens. One further probe pass certifies the exact order-marginalized MAP set. Across four document-disjoint splits and two scales on the primary MetaX device, compiled control matches the serial policy on $84$--$89\%$ of questions --- every instrumented divergence a floating-point near-tie --- and cuts control latency by $35$--$47\%$ versus token-wise serial decoding and $6$--$7\%$ versus an idealized chunked engine; an H800 repetition preserves the ordering.
papers.title_zh: 将自回归LLM控制编译为面向分层RAG的策略精确并行推理
papers.abstract_zh: 大语言模型越来越多地在结构化决策流水线中充当控制器，然而其决策仍由自回归文本解码来执行。分层RAG就是这样一个场景：在文档树的每个前沿，一个LLM在依赖输入的动作文法下确定选择$k$个章节中的$b$个，其执行方式要么是易出错的自由形式JSON，要么是可靠但严格串行的文法约束生成。我们表明，对于有界时域控制，这种串行化是不必要的：可达未来形成一棵浅层动作前缀树，我们对其进行编译——一次根预填充加上一次树因果探测，使用与串行解码相同的词元、位置和因果祖先来评估每个以前缀为条件的动作分布。一个前缀状态引理使编译后的控制在精确算术下达到策略精确：它实现同一策略，具有两次前向的关键路径和零输出词元。额外一次探测遍历可认证精确的顺序边缘化MAP集合。在主要MetaX设备上的四个文档不相交划分和两种规模上，编译后的控制在$84$--$89\%$的问题上与串行策略一致——每个经插桩检测的差异都是浮点近似平局——并将控制延迟相较于逐词元串行解码降低$35$--$47\%$，相较于理想化的分块引擎降低$6$--$7\%$；在H800上的重复实验保持了这一排序。

papers.title: Spectral Smoothing and Spiking Perturbations Reconfigure Capability Profiles and Selective Task Performance in Large Language Models
papers.summary: Singular-value spectra encode important structure in transformer feed-forward projections, yet their causal role in downstream behavior remains underexplored. We study post-hoc spectral smoothing and spiking interventions on the up_proj and down_proj matrices. Positive perturbation stretches deviations from the geometric mean, making large singular values larger and small ones smaller (spiking), and vice versa. The intervention preserves singular vectors and the geometric mean of the singular values. Across five open Llama and Qwen instruction models, we evaluate the perturbed systems on capability-labeled subtasks, standard and chain-of-thought reasoning benchmarks, judge-scored truthfulness, hallucination, and safety tasks, and TRAIT personality probes. To interpret score shifts, we fit responses in a three-dimensional capability basis consisting of factual knowledge, language understanding, and deductive reasoning. The induced changes suggest structured rather than purely random sensitivity: large positive perturbations more reliably suppress language and deductive responses, moderate negative perturbations can sometimes improve factual or task-local performance on the evaluated grids, and sensitivity varies strongly by model family, benchmark module, and underlying layerwise spectral inequality. These results position spectral perturbation as a lightweight intervention for probing how capabilities are organized and traded off in large language models.
papers.title_zh: 谱平滑与尖峰扰动重构大型语言模型的能力轮廓与选择性任务表现
papers.abstract_zh: 奇异值谱编码了 transformer 前馈投影中的重要结构，但其在下游行为中的因果作用仍未被充分探索。我们研究对 up_proj 和 down_proj 矩阵的事后谱平滑与尖峰干预。正扰动拉伸相对于几何均值的偏差，使大奇异值更大、小奇异值更小（尖峰化），反之亦然。该干预保持奇异向量以及奇异值的几何均值不变。在五个开源的 Llama 和 Qwen 指令模型上，我们在能力标注的子任务、标准与思维链推理基准、由评判器评分的真实性、幻觉与安全任务，以及 TRAIT 人格探测上评估受扰系统。为解释分数变化，我们将响应拟合到由事实知识、语言理解和演绎推理构成的三维能力基中。所引发的变化表明存在结构化而非纯随机的敏感性：大幅正扰动更可靠地抑制语言与演绎响应，中等负扰动有时可在所评估的网格上改善事实性或任务局部表现，且敏感性因模型家族、基准模块以及底层逐层谱不等性而显著变化。这些结果将谱扰动定位为一种轻量级干预手段，用于探究大型语言模型中能力如何组织与权衡。

papers.title: WikiOriginQA: Automated Construction of a QA Dataset with Knowledge Origins for Analyzing Cultural Bias
papers.summary: Existing datasets on cultural knowledge have been typically created by human annotators familiar with each culture. However, the process requires considerable human effort, presenting a significant challenge to scalability. To address this challenge, we introduce WikiOriginQA, a QA dataset automatically constructed by objectively representing the origins of knowledge through the creation dates of different Wikipedia language editions. Experimental results with the created dataset confirm that LLM performance tends to be biased toward Anglophone cultures. Furthermore, the results suggest the importance of knowledge propagation into the Anglosphere. These findings demonstrate the validity of our automated approach, enabling cultural bias evaluations with superior scalability across diverse languages without extensive manual annotation.

papers.title: Direct cueing of word identity through word duration: evidence from Mandarin homophones
papers.summary: While there is increasing evidence that words are stored in the mental lexicon with some phonetic detail, there are open questions about exactly which phonetic details are stored and whether they are functionally relevant for spoken word recognition. Word-level phonetic cues, such as word duration, provide an appropriate test case. Across languages, including Mandarin Chinese, high frequency words are shorter than low frequency words. Using a homophone ordering task, we investigate whether differences in word duration impact word recognition. Mandarin Chinese was examined since it has abundant disyllabic homophones. Our results indicate that participants were able to use word duration to recognize the order of homophone pairs, selected to vary in lexical frequency. Both with high noise levels and when no other cues were available, participants mapped the shorter duration auditory stimulus to the higher frequency word. The results provide evidence that word duration can directly cue the identity of words, suggesting that it may be a phonetic detail incorporated into the lexical representation. We discuss this direct cueing account alongside alternative accounts of how word duration may modulate word recognition.

papers.title: From Clinical Judgment to Checkable Rules: Clinician-Led Guardrails for Mental-Health Chatbots
papers.summary: Large language models (LLMs) deployed in mental-health contexts can be evaluated for safety failures, but the resulting judgments are often difficult to inspect or explain. Common approaches to improving safety rely on prompt engineering, LLM-as-a-Judge, and Constitutional AI. In this work, we describe a clinician-led alternative in which two clinicians define, finalize, and adjudicate the four safety checks of a rule base, which is formally verified for internal consistency and applied as a guardrail over LLM outputs. Here and in the title, clinician-led refers to this rule base, not to the fact extractor or the uncertainty default, which are ours. Every verdict of the resulting verification layer is recomputable from a named rule and sixteen facts. Against an LLM judge matched in model, revision, quantization, rule text, and decoding but without the layer's computed 988/911 fact, the largest disagreement class, the satisfied-rule class, is structured: the Llama-3.3-70B judge, on its primary prompt, demands a crisis resource from 55 of the 65 replies (84.6%) that already contain one, while the same model, asked as a fact extractor, reports a recognized resource present on 54 of the 55. The verification layer never raises that demand, by construction. We report with equal prominence where this judge is stronger: fewer false crisis alarms on the one reference-scored check. We also report the measured cost (a specification revision raised block-class outcomes on held-out boundary prompts of an over-refusal benchmark from 6.0% to 16.0%, chiefly by changing fact extraction), the clinicians' decision to keep our uncertainty default, and the analysis of the result. The contribution is not a safer verdict. It is a guardrail whose disagreements with the judge localize to named rules and facts and whose measured costs trace to named facts and the uncertainty default.
papers.title_zh: 从临床判断到可核查规则：临床医生主导的心理健康聊天机器人护栏
papers.abstract_zh: 部署在心理健康情境中的大型语言模型（LLMs）可以因安全失败而受到评估，但由此产生的判断往往难以检查或解释。提高安全性的常见方法依赖于提示工程、以LLM作为评判者以及宪法式AI。在本工作中，我们描述了一种临床医生主导的替代方案：两名临床医生定义、最终确定并裁定一个规则库的四项安全检查，该规则库经形式化验证以确保内部一致性，并作为LLM输出之上的护栏加以应用。在本文和标题中，“临床医生主导”指的是该规则库，而不是事实提取器或不确定性默认值——后两者由我们负责。由此产生的验证层的每一个判定都可以从一条具名规则和十六个事实重新计算。与一个在模型、修订版本、量化、规则文本和解码上均匹配、但不具备该层计算出的988/911事实的LLM评判器相比，最大的分歧类别——满足规则类——是有结构的：Llama-3.3-70B评判器在其主提示下，对65条已经包含危机资源的回复中的55条（84.6%）要求提供危机资源，而同一模型作为事实提取器被询问时，报告在55条中有54条存在已识别的资源。验证层从构造上绝不会提出该要求。我们同等突出地报告该评判器更强的地方：在唯一一个以参考评分的检查上，虚假危机警报更少。我们还报告了测量到的成本（一次规范修订将过度拒绝基准的留出边界提示上的block类结果从6.0%提高到16.0%，主要是通过改变事实提取），临床医生保留我们的不确定性默认值的决定，以及对结果的分析。贡献不是一个更安全的判定。它是一道护栏，其与评判器的分歧可定位到具名规则和事实，其测量到的成本可追溯到具名事实和不确定性默认值。

papers.title: ULME: Predictive Coupling for Mutually Reinforcing Embedding and Language Modeling
papers.summary: Text embedding and text generation are two of the most useful capabilities of modern large language models, yet they are typically provided by separate specialized models (an embedder and a generator) trained with incompatible objectives and deployed side by side in retrieval-augmented generation and agent systems. Recent unified embedding-generation models such as GritLM share parameters between the two capabilities, but they either switch attention regimes between modes or optimize embedding and language modeling as parallel objectives that never supervise each other. We argue that these designs are only partially unified: the two capabilities coexist on the same weights, but do not shape each other. We propose ULME, a post-training framework that unifies embedding and language modeling on a causal decoder-only LLM through predictive coupling. ULME inserts a chain of learnable slots between the query and the answer, reads a semantic embedding and a reasoning embedding from two designated slots, and trains three objectives on a shared causal backbone: a contrastive loss anchoring the semantic slot to document representations, a language-modeling loss supervising answer generation, and a stop-gradient predictive loss that aligns the reasoning slot with a pooled summary of the answer, so that generation actively shapes what the embedding encodes. Across two model families (Qwen2.5, Qwen3) and eight scales spanning 0.5B-8B parameters, a single ULME checkpoint improves MTEB by 3.3-4.1 points over the strongest open-source baseline, tightens BRIGHT and AdvBench-IR simultaneously, and remains on par with a generation-only fine-tune on standard accuracy benchmarks (MMLU, GSM8K, MMLU-Pro, HumanEval), demonstrating that genuine unification yields mutually reinforcing rather than merely coexisting capabilities.
papers.title_zh: ULME：用于相互增强的嵌入与语言建模的预测耦合
papers.abstract_zh: 文本嵌入与文本生成是现代大语言模型两项最有用的能力，但它们通常由分别训练的专用模型（一个嵌入器和一个生成器）提供，这些模型以互不兼容的目标进行训练，并在检索增强生成和智能体系统中并排部署。近期诸如 GritLM 之类的统一嵌入-生成模型在两种能力之间共享参数，但它们要么在两种模式之间切换注意力机制，要么将嵌入和语言建模作为从不相互监督的并行目标进行优化。我们认为这些设计只是部分统一：两种能力共存于同一组权重之上，但并不会相互塑造。我们提出 ULME，一个后训练框架，它通过预测耦合在仅解码器的因果大语言模型上统一嵌入和语言建模。ULME 在查询与答案之间插入一串可学习的槽位，从两个指定槽位读取语义嵌入和推理嵌入，并在共享的因果主干上训练三个目标：一个将语义槽位锚定到文档表示的对比损失、一个监督答案生成的语言建模损失，以及一个将推理槽位与答案的池化摘要对齐的停止梯度预测损失，从而使生成主动塑造嵌入所编码的内容。在两个模型系列（Qwen2.5、Qwen3）和跨越 0.5B-8B 参数的八个规模上，单个 ULME 检查点相较最强的开源基线将 MTEB 提升 3.3-4.1 分，同时收紧 BRIGHT 和 AdvBench-IR，并在标准准确率基准（MMLU、GSM8K、MMLU-Pro、HumanEval）上与仅生成微调保持相当，证明真正的统一产生的是相互增强而非仅仅共存的能力。

papers.title: Meaning Contracts: Local Semantic Geometry in Large Language Models
papers.summary: This paper studies the local geometry of semantic meaning in large language models. Current representation analyses ask whether meanings are close in embedding space, or whether linear probes separate semantic classes, but they do not characterize the within-concept local geometry: what is invariant across realizations of a single semantic factor, what varies, and what changes when meaning is refined. This paper characterizes that geometry through two controlled probes evaluated on four architecturally diverse decoder-only LLMs (Gemma 4, Llama 3.2, Qwen 2.5, Pythia). A cross-lingual probe uses language as a perturbation to separate exact meaning matches, same-factor realizations, nearby concepts, and out-of-domain contrasts. A refinement probe separates specificity-bearing semantic narrowing from high-probability attributive elaboration and adversarial controls; both probes are validated by blind human judgments. Four findings recur across all models: under mean pooling, once dominant variance directions are removed, sentence pairs order by semantic relatedness (same factor, then same domain, then different domain) without overlap over a band of layers; semantic factors organize around an invariant core surrounded by structured realization-specific variation; refinement produces directed displacement into tighter neighborhoods, including against controls built on the same base noun; and sentence-level and token-local readouts expose complementary geometry (volume contraction at the sentence level, sharper anisotropic endpoints at token-local readout). We interpret these results as evidence that LLM semantics are organized as local anisotropic neighborhoods in which meaning contracts under refinement.
papers.title_zh: 意义收缩：大语言模型中的局部语义几何
papers.abstract_zh: 本文研究大语言模型中语义含义的局部几何。当前的表示分析询问含义在嵌入空间中是否接近，或线性探针是否能分离语义类别，但它们并未刻画概念内部的局部几何：在单一语义因子的不同实现中什么是保持不变的，什么发生变化，以及当含义被细化时什么发生改变。本文通过两个受控探针在四个架构各异的仅解码器大语言模型（Gemma 4、Llama 3.2、Qwen 2.5、Pythia）上评估，来刻画该几何。跨语言探针将语言作为扰动，以区分精确含义匹配、同一因子的不同实现、邻近概念以及域外对比。细化探针将承载特异性的语义窄化与高概率的定语性扩展以及对抗性对照区分开来；两个探针均通过盲人类判断得到验证。四项发现在所有模型中反复出现：在均值池化下，一旦移除主导方差方向，句子对便按语义相关性排序（同一因子，然后是同一领域，再是不同领域），并在一段层范围内没有重叠；语义因子围绕一个不变核心组织，该核心被结构化的、特定于实现的变化所包围；细化产生指向更紧密邻域的有向位移，包括相对于基于同一基础名词构建的对照；并且句子级和词元局部的读出暴露出互补的几何结构（句子级的体积收缩，词元局部读出下更尖锐的各向异性端点）。我们将这些结果解释为证据，表明大语言模型的语义被组织为局部各向异性邻域，在其中含义在细化下发生收缩。

papers.title: UniGuard: Multi-View Guardrail Learning for Cross-Interface Safety Generalization
papers.summary: Guardrail models are increasingly used as safety layers for LLMs and agentic systems, but most are trained on fixed prompt or response interfaces and become unreliable when the same safety case appears as a conversation, agent trajectory, multi-agent trace, or policy-conditioned input. We propose UniGuard, a training framework that learns interface-invariant safety representations from multiple semantically aligned views of the same safety case. We also construct the UniGuard-FT dataset by transforming 1,000 public safety cases into prompt, response, multi-turn conversation, agent-trace, and multi-agent-trace views, and train UniGuard-0.6B with classification, supervised contrastive learning, and asymmetric confidence calibration losses. Across unseen-interface benchmarks ATBench, PolicyGuardBench, and DynaBench, UniGuard-0.6B improves over its pretrained guardrail by 45.12 F1 points on average and reduces expected calibration error by 35.41 points, while remaining competitive with much larger guardrails such as Claude-Sonnet-4.5 and GPT-5.2 - despite being a 0.6B model and trained only with synthetic data.

papers.title: Where meanings converge and diverge: Revisiting linguistic relativity across 81 languages
papers.summary: Do people who speak different languages organize concepts in similar ways? This question lies at the heart of the Sapir--Whorf hypothesis and debates about linguistic relativity. Shared basic meanings, however, need not imply shared relations among them. We compared relations among 196 basic concepts across 81 languages, using word embeddings from two multilingual models to quantify conceptual structure expressed in language. Cross-language correspondence was greater for sociocultural meanings than for meanings concerning nature and motion, a contrast recurring across models and classifications. Within the sociocultural domain, relational differences increased with geographic separation; less closely related languages differed more across all domains. These findings suggest that universality and relativity are interwoven across conceptual domains. They inform an account in which shared cognitive resources interact with linguistic and local experience, and predict greater cross-language correspondence in human semantic judgments for sociocultural than for nature and motion meanings.

papers.title: Invisibilization as a Source of Probability Bias in Language Models
papers.summary: Language models are aligned to avoid using protected attributes such as race, ethnicity, and gender to inform their responses. Therefore, they increasingly refuse or hedge when such attributes appear in a prompt. However, if a system must decide how much to learn from what people tell it, it is costly to refuse valuable information because of its source. In this article, we measure the cost of declining information in a two-urn game with an exact Bayesian answer. We present leading LLM models from two developers (OpenAI and Anthropic) with a prompt that requires them to decide how far to trust an unverifiable report from a participant whose description we randomize across ten configurations (6,600 sessions). We show that leading models often decline to assess the reporter, treating information as worthless at rates set by the description rather than by the evidence. At its widest, models decline a Black-described reporter 46% of the time and a white-described reporter 9%; yet, when they do assess the information, the Black-described reporter receives slightly more trust. The bias is invisible to audits that compare average trust or look only at assessed cases. It grows with reasoning effort, follows words rather than categories (models invoke race for "Black" but not for its Spanish translation negro, and never for "Indigenous"), and worsens under warning instructions a practitioner would try first. We also present a scoring option that reduces the refusal rate bias. When a model's trust is scored against revealed truth over repeated rounds, it credits identical records equally. In four of five configurations from Anthropic and OpenAI, the racial gap in trust falls below 0.02 by the last rounds.

papers.title: TutorCaseBench: A Case-Grounded Benchmark for Evaluating LLM Tutors in Supporting Students with Challenging Behaviors
papers.summary: LLMs are increasingly used as AI tutors, yet existing benchmarks overlook the challenging behaviors common among students with learning and behavioral difficulties. We introduce TutorCaseBench, a benchmark that grounds AI-tutor evaluation in qualitative case studies from pedagogy, educational psychology, and special education. Our pipeline converts documented student categories into case-specific scenarios, tutor-student dialogues, and rubrics grounded in source evidence. The benchmark contains 923 dialogues across five challenge types, evaluated through open-ended response generation (1,560 items) and multiple-choice selection (2,537 items). Across 11 state-of-the-art LLMs, even the strongest model satisfies a rubric criterion in only 55.8% of open-ended cases, while models are better at selecting appropriate strategies than generating situated responses. These results reveal a gap between intervention recognition and context-specific adaptation, especially for open-weight models. All data are publicly available at https://github.com/kixlab/TutorCaseBench.

papers.title: TRIAD: Benchmarking Omni-Modal Ambiguity in Multimodal Large Language Models
papers.summary: Ambiguity is a central feature of natural communication: a sentence, image, or sound may remain underspecified until evidence from the other channels is considered. Yet current multimodal benchmarks mostly test perception, recognition, or reasoning over already determinate inputs, leaving unclear whether omni-modal large language models can resolve ambiguity distributed across text, vision, and audio. We introduce TRIAD, a benchmark for omni-modal ambiguity resolution. Each item is a text--image--audio triplet paired with a question and a set of answer options, and is constructed so that the full triplet determines a unique answer while removing any one modality makes the set of consistent options non-unique. TRIAD contains $327$ hand-written queries in $86$ scene groups and covers $18$ ambiguity categories across the three modalities. Evaluating $14$ omni-modal systems reveals that strong item-level performance does not translate into robust scene-level disambiguation: the best model still trails humans by over $20$ points in group accuracy. Removing answer options widens the gap further, driving model group accuracy to the single digits while humans remain robust. Leave-one-out and transcript/description counterfactuals further show that current systems often underuse audio cues when text and image are present. TRIAD reframes omni-modal evaluation around disambiguation rather than recognition, and provides a taxonomy, benchmark, and diagnostic protocol for measuring this capability.
papers.title_zh: TRIAD：对多模态大语言模型中的全模态歧义进行基准测试
papers.abstract_zh: 歧义是自然交流的核心特征：一个句子、图像或声音在考虑来自其他通道的证据之前可能仍然是欠确定的。然而，当前的多模态基准大多测试对已经确定的输入的感知、识别或推理，这使得全模态大语言模型是否能够解决分布在文本、视觉和音频中的歧义仍不清楚。我们引入 TRIAD，一个用于全模态歧义解决的基准。每个条目是一个文本--图像--音频三元组，配有一个问题和一组答案选项，并且其构造使得完整三元组确定一个唯一答案，而移除任一模态都会使一致的选项集合变得不唯一。TRIAD 包含 $327$ 个手写查询，分为 $86$ 个场景组，并覆盖三种模态上的 $18$ 个歧义类别。评估 $14$ 个全模态系统表明，强大的条目级性能并不能转化为稳健的场景级消歧：最佳模型在组准确率上仍落后人类超过 $20$ 个百分点。移除答案选项会进一步扩大差距，使模型的组准确率降至个位数，而人类仍保持稳健。留一法和转写/描述反事实进一步表明，当前系统在文本和图像存在时常常未充分利用音频线索。TRIAD 将全模态评估重新围绕消歧而非识别，并提供了用于衡量这一能力的分类体系、基准和诊断协议。

papers.title: Synthetic-to-Real Code-Switched ASR: A Spontaneous Nepali-English Podcast Benchmark
papers.summary: Nepali-English code-switched conversational speech presents severe challenges for automatic speech recognition (ASR), chiefly through script confusion (inappropriate mixing of Devanagari and Latin orthography) and elevated error rates at language switch points. Supervised fine-tuning (SFT) can adapt multilingual foundation models, but human code-switched audio is expensive to collect and annotate. We curate a new benchmark of 13,044 spontaneous podcast utterances (15.45 h total; 10,214 test, 2,830 dev), audited and verified to eliminate machine translation leakages and acoustic loops. We investigate a two-stage synthetic-to-real adaptation framework: Stage 1 applies SFT on 0.95 h of speech synthesized via a multi-speaker, dual-engine TTS pipeline; Stage 2 explores Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) with transcription and script rewards. We find that synthetic SFT provides the primary cross-domain transfer to spontaneous human speech, reducing Mixed Error Rate (MER) from 23.40% to 21.52% (-1.88 pp) and switch-point error rate (SPER) from 35.89% to 28.77% (-7.12 pp). Subsequent GRPO yields small, statistically significant adjustments on 173 test utterances (1.69%), driving English script confusion (SCR_en) from 6.45% to 6.36% (p <= 0.001) and SPER to 28.70% (p = 0.022 clustered). Crucially, ablation reveals that in this SFT-converged encoder-decoder setting, an auxiliary script reward term yields performance identical to MER-only optimization because rollout candidate groups exhibit near-zero script variance on synthetic data. On monolingual benchmarks, SFT improves Nepali MER by 2.71 pp (stabilizing at 18.42% after GRPO, a 2.38 pp gain over baseline) while preserving English lexical WER (3.38% vs. 3.33%). Verified transcripts, timestamps, episode metadata, and reconstruction scripts are publicly released.

papers.title: From Perpetrators' Digital Footprints to Behavioral Communities: An Ontology-Driven Framework for Bengali Cyberbullying Analysis--- FULL VERSION
papers.summary: Cyberbullying involves behavioral and contextual patterns beyond isolated abusive messages. However, existing approaches remain fragmented across content detection, semantic representation, and network analysis, with limited interpretable perpetrator representations, multi-scale structural modeling, and explanations of behavior-driven similarity and influence propagation. These limitations hinder the identification of persistent perpetrators, characterization of behavioral communities, and assessment of potentially influential users. This paper proposes Ontology-Driven Cyberbullying Behavior and Network Analysis (ODCBNA), a perpetrator-centric framework integrating requirements-driven ontology design, knowledge graph construction, behavioral modeling, community analysis, and influence modeling. Using the Bengali Contextual and Diverse Cyberbullying (BenCoDiC) corpus as a use case, ODCBNA identifies $1{,}063$ users with at least three bullying comments or replies as perpetrators and represents each through a $64$-dimensional behavioral and contextual feature vector. Cosine similarity and $k$-nearest-neighbor modeling produce a weighted network with $27{,}554$ edges. Louvain analysis identifies six communities with a modularity of approximately $0.495$ and $27$ sub-communities. Feature-contribution analysis identifies the Video, Impact, and User Profile groups as the strongest contributors to behavioral similarity and community separation, while contextual dimensions support interpretation. Community-constrained influence analysis shows that IM Greedy achieves small positive gains in all six communities, although different seed-selection methods produce comparable diffusion spreads despite limited seed overlap. These findings provide an interpretable basis for understanding perpetrator behavior, community organization, and potential influence patterns in Bengali online environments.
papers.title_zh: 从施害者的数字足迹到行为社群：一种本体驱动的孟加拉语网络欺凌分析框架——完整版
papers.abstract_zh: 网络欺凌涉及超越孤立辱骂性消息的行为与情境模式。然而，现有方法在内容检测、语义表示和网络分析方面仍然相互割裂，并且对施害者的可解释表示、多尺度结构建模以及行为驱动相似性和影响传播的解释仍然有限。这些局限阻碍了对持续施害者的识别、对行为社群的刻画以及对潜在有影响力用户的评估。本文提出本体驱动的网络欺凌行为与网络分析（Ontology-Driven Cyberbullying Behavior and Network Analysis，ODCBNA），这是一个以施害者为中心的框架，集成了需求驱动的本体设计、知识图谱构建、行为建模、社群分析和影响建模。以孟加拉语情境化与多样化网络欺凌（Bengali Contextual and Diverse Cyberbullying，BenCoDiC）语料库为用例，ODCBNA 将至少有三条欺凌评论或回复的 $1{,}063$ 名用户识别为施害者，并通过 $64$ 维行为与情境特征向量表示每一名施害者。余弦相似度和 $k$ 最近邻建模生成一个具有 $27{,}554$ 条边的加权网络。Louvain 分析识别出六个社群，模块度约为 $0.495$，并识别出 $27$ 个子社群。特征贡献分析识别出 Video、Impact 和 User Profile 组是行为相似性和社群分离的最强贡献者，而情境维度支持解释。社群约束下的影响分析表明，IM Greedy 在所有六个社群中均取得小幅正向增益，尽管不同种子选择方法在种子重叠有限的情况下仍产生可比的扩散范围。这些发现为理解孟加拉语在线环境中的施害者行为、社群组织和潜在影响模式提供了可解释的基础。

papers.title: Silicon Samples Match the Answers but Not the Respondents
papers.summary: Silicon sampling generates survey respondents by having a large language model (LLM) answer a survey as a person with given demographic attributes, and the resulting synthetic populations are increasingly used in place of human ones. Existing evaluations focus on individual-answer accuracy, per-question answer distributions, and correlations across questions. None of these compares the respondents themselves, so a generator whose respondents have combinations of answers found in no human respondent can still score well if it reproduces every answer distribution. We propose the respondent coverage gap (RCG), which represents each respondent as a point defined by their complete answer profile and measures how far each human respondent is from the nearest generated one, relative to the distance between human samples. On two US social surveys, all six LLMs we evaluate leave human respondents uncovered, and under our main settings, they fall behind a baseline that samples each answer independently from the human marginals. Across the prompting and inference settings we test, every LLM has a higher RCG than a Gaussian copula fitted to the human data.
papers.title_zh: 硅样本匹配答案，但不匹配受访者
papers.abstract_zh: 硅采样通过让大语言模型（LLM）以具有给定人口统计属性的人的身份回答调查来生成调查受访者，由此得到的合成人群正越来越多地被用于替代人类人群。现有评估聚焦于个体答案准确率、逐题答案分布以及问题之间的相关性。这些评估都没有比较受访者本身，因此，如果一个生成器所生成的受访者具有在人类受访者中找不到的答案组合，只要它复现了每一个答案分布，仍然可以获得良好评分。我们提出受访者覆盖差距（RCG），它将每个受访者表示为由其完整答案画像定义的一个点，并衡量每个人类受访者到最近生成受访者的距离，且该距离是相对于人类样本之间的距离而言的。在两个美国社会调查上，我们评估的全部六个LLM都使人类受访者未被覆盖，并且在我们主要设置下，它们落后于一个从人类边际分布中独立抽取每个答案的基线。在我们测试的提示和推理设置中，每个LLM的RCG都高于拟合人类数据的高斯 copula。

papers.title: ReflectPO: Reflection-Guided Policy Optimization for Long-Horizon LLM Agents
papers.summary: With external tools, large language models (LLMs) can tackle complex tasks through sustained environmental interaction. LLM-based agents are therefore increasingly used to tackle complex long-horizon tasks in real-world environments. However, these tasks involve sequential, interdependent decisions and changes in environmental states. Early execution errors affect subsequent interaction histories and environmental states, and their effects accumulate along the decision chain. To address this challenge, we propose Reflection-Guided Policy Optimization (ReflectPO), a reinforcement learning framework for autonomous error recovery in long-horizon tasks. ReflectPO comprises two core components. The first is Reflection-Guided Sampling. We use branch differences and repeated visits in interaction trajectories to construct hints for error recovery. The second is Tree-Structured Credit Assignment. We organize sampled trajectories into trees and assign action-level credit using parent--child reward differences and recovery gains. Experiments over two long-horizon tool-use benchmarks show that ReflectPO outperforms multiple existing baselines in most domains. It also achieves the best overall performance on average. Further analyses show that ReflectPO effectively improves agents' ability to recognize their own deviations, recover from erroneous states, and continue making progress toward task completion.
papers.title_zh: ReflectPO：面向长时程LLM智能体的反思引导策略优化
papers.abstract_zh: 借助外部工具，大型语言模型（LLMs）能够通过持续的环境交互来完成复杂任务。因此，基于LLM的智能体越来越多地被用于处理真实世界环境中的复杂长时程任务。然而，这些任务涉及序列化、相互依赖的决策以及环境状态的变化。早期的执行错误会影响后续的交互历史和环境状态，并且其影响会沿决策链累积。为应对这一挑战，我们提出反思引导策略优化（ReflectPO），一种用于长时程任务中自主错误恢复的强化学习框架。ReflectPO包含两个核心组件。第一个是反思引导采样。我们利用交互轨迹中的分支差异和重复访问来构造用于错误恢复的提示。第二个是树结构信用分配。我们将采样得到的轨迹组织为树，并利用父—子奖励差异和恢复增益来分配动作级信用。在两个长时程工具使用基准上的实验表明，ReflectPO在大多数领域中优于多个现有基线。它在平均整体性能上也取得了最佳表现。进一步的分析表明，ReflectPO有效提升了智能体识别自身偏差、从错误状态中恢复并继续朝着任务完成取得进展的能力。

papers.title: Verbalizing Activation Differences with Natural Language Autoencoders
papers.summary: Activation verbalizers translate the internal representations of large language models into human-readable text. The recently proposed natural language autoencoders (NLAs) learn this by reconstructing activations through a natural language bottleneck. However, it remains unclear how well these methods generalize beyond the setting they were trained for. Here, we study this question for NLAs along four closely related questions: (i) Do NLA verbalizations exhibit compositional structure with respect to their input? (ii) Do NLAs generalize to finetuned versions of the model they were trained for? (iii) Can NLAs recover finetuning objectives in model diffing? (iv) Can NLAs be specialized for model diffing? Across four models from three families, our experiments provide evidence supporting a largely positive answer to all four questions. Specifically, verbalizations of composed analogy activations mostly name the target while rarely mentioning the subtracted word, and an NLA can be reused on lightweight finetunes of its original model without retraining, with reconstruction quality degrading noticeably only for the largest model. Verbalizing activation differences between Taboo model organisms and their original models recovers the concealed secret word for most organisms, and reinforcement learning on activation differences further improves this recovery on held-out organisms. We also find that NLAs can recover the finetuning objective without the finetuned model generating any token, since the most informative token positions precede the user prompt. NLAs do not yet match state-of-the-art model diffing methods on the emergent misalignment detection task, but outperform a blackbox baseline. Our findings suggest that NLAs can meaningfully verbalize differences in activation space, rendering NLAs a promising direction for future work.
papers.title_zh: 用自然语言自编码器言语化激活差异
papers.abstract_zh: 激活言语化器将大语言模型的内部表示转换为人类可读的文本。最近提出的自然语言自编码器（NLAs）通过自然语言瓶颈重建激活来学习这一点。然而，这些方法在超出其训练设定之后能泛化到什么程度仍不清楚。在这里，我们围绕四个密切相关的问题，针对 NLAs 研究这一问题：(i) NLA 的言语化结果是否相对于其输入表现出组合结构？(ii) NLAs 是否能泛化到其所训练模型的微调版本？(iii) NLAs 能否在模型差异分析中恢复微调目标？(iv) NLAs 能否专门化用于模型差异分析？在来自三个模型族的四个模型上，我们的实验提供了证据，支持对全部四个问题给出很大程度上肯定的回答。具体而言，对组合类比激活的言语化大多会说出目标，而很少提及被减去的词；并且一个 NLA 可以在无需重新训练的情况下复用于其原始模型的轻量级微调版本，重建质量仅在最大模型上明显下降。对 Taboo 模型生物体与其原始模型之间的激活差异进行言语化，能够为大多数生物体恢复隐藏的秘密词，而对激活差异进行强化学习进一步改善了在留出生物体上的这种恢复。我们还发现，NLAs 可以在微调模型不生成任何 token 的情况下恢复微调目标，因为信息量最大的 token 位置位于用户提示之前。在涌现性错位检测任务上，NLAs 尚未达到最先进的模型差异分析方法的水平，但优于黑箱基线。我们的发现表明，NLAs 能够有意义地对激活空间中的差异进行言语化，使 NLAs 成为未来工作的一个有前景的方向。

papers.title: RetiJev: Fast and Source-Grounded Ophthalmic Decision Models
papers.summary: Ophthalmic clinical decision support requires fast, accurate, and privacy-preserving inference, yet autoregressive large language models (LLMs) incur substantial latency and computational overhead for decisions among predefined actions. We therefore investigate a decision-oriented alternative to generative reasoning. Specifically, we first introduce RetiJev-Data, a source-grounded ophthalmology corpus comprising 78,158 clinical-decision and diagnosis questions derived from articles in PubMed Central and a MeSH vocabulary covering 531 eye diseases, and 50,074 guideline-grading questions spanning 11 grading systems, along with a 24,662-question evaluation benchmark. Based on this, we develop RetiJev, a family of 0.8B-9B decision models that directly score candidate answers without autoregressive decoding. Across all model sizes, RetiJev outperforms both a 27B LLM and the commercial Jev 1.13 decision model on guideline grading by 10.4-23.0 points. RetiJev-9B further achieves the highest accuracy on clinical decisions, improving over both baselines by 5.4-6.5 points while matching them on diagnosis. It answers a case in 158 ms on one GPU, 3.5x faster than LLM generation and 470x faster than reasoning. Models are released at https://github.com/Awenbocc/RetiJev.
papers.title_zh: RetiJev：快速且基于来源的眼科决策模型
papers.abstract_zh: 眼科临床决策支持需要快速、准确且隐私保护的推理，然而自回归大语言模型（LLMs）在预定义动作之间进行决策时会产生显著的延迟和计算开销。因此，我们研究了一种面向决策的生成式推理替代方案。具体而言，我们首先介绍了 RetiJev-Data，这是一个基于来源的眼科语料库，包含 78,158 个源自 PubMed Central 文章和覆盖 531 种眼病的 MeSH 词表的临床决策与诊断问题，以及跨越 11 个分级系统的 50,074 个指南分级问题，并附带一个包含 24,662 个问题的评估基准。基于此，我们开发了 RetiJev，这是一系列 0.8B-9B 的决策模型，无需自回归解码即可直接对候选答案评分。在所有模型规模上，RetiJev 在指南分级上均比一个 27B LLM 和商业 Jev 1.13 决策模型高出 10.4-23.0 分。RetiJev-9B 进一步在临床决策上取得最高准确率，较两个基线提高 5.4-6.5 分，同时在诊断上与它们持平。它在单块 GPU 上回答一个病例仅需 158 ms，比 LLM 生成快 3.5 倍，比推理快 470 倍。模型发布于 https://github.com/Awenbocc/RetiJev。

papers.title: IQuest-Q1: Advancing Foundation Capabilities for Agentic CLI Systems
papers.summary: We present IQuest-Q1, a sparse Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) agentic foundation model with 320B total parameters (15B activated).
